newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Industry Council to focus on information society.
newsitem.headline: Industry Council to focus on information society.

text.p: The Industry Council will devote its entire session on Tuesday in Luxembourg to discussions about EU policies aimed at promoting the information society.

Three commissioners -- Martin Bangemann (telecommunications and information technologies), Mario Monti (internal market) and Padraig Flynn (social affairs) -- will attend the meeting to present five recent Commission initiatives in the sector, EU officials said.

The Council will then try to agree a resolution setting out EU priorities for a new action plan on the information society that the Commission plans to present to the Dublin European Council in December.

"It's mostly a focus Council," an Irish presidency source said, noting that a wide range of policy areas come into play, from telecommunications and intellectual property to social policy and the internal market.

The ministers will also hold a meeting with their counterparts from 10 central and east European countries (CEECs) as part of the "structured dialogue" that is meant to pave the way for the countries' eventual EU membership.
The discussion will build on the outcome of the EU-CEEC Forum on the Information Society that took place in September in Prague.

The Irish presidency is hoping to involve EU states in an action plan that was agreed at the conference setting out 27 ideas for computer and telecommunications pilot projects in areas such as transport, education, medicine and research.
"Clearly there are opportunities for West European industries," the Irish source said.
The six initiatives that will be presented by the Commission are:
-- Communication on "The implications of the information society for European Union policies", COM(96)395
-- Communication on "Standardization and the global information society: the European approach", COM(96)359
-- Green paper on "Living and working in the information society: people first", COM(96)389
-- Communication on "Learning in the Information Society"
-- Draft directive setting up a "transparency mechanism" requiring member states to notify the Commission before adopting rules affecting information society services, COM(96)392.
The Council resolution will guide the Commission as it updates its July 1994 action plan on the information society, COM(94)347.
